[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-11.05): Good morning, Elaine. Marcus Lim here. Thanks for setting aside time for our call. Are you somewhere you can speak privately, or would another time be more convenient?
[seg_0002] Client (11.45-22.66): Morning, Marcus. I'm in my office with the door closed, so now is fine. Telephone is still easiest for me. Between the business and things at home, I don't always get to my emails promptly.
[seg_0003] Advisor (23.05-32.00): Certainly, we'll keep it concise. Before we get into the discussion, please provide your identification details for telephone verification.
[seg_0004] Client (32.40-39.31): My NRIC is S six three six seven eight oh one L. My date of birth is the twenty-first of January nineteen eighty-three.
[seg_0005] Advisor (39.72-46.88): Thank you. How has your gardening been going? Last time you mentioned spending some of your weekend outside.
[seg_0006] Client (47.27-56.52): Quite nicely, actually. I've been repotting my herbs and clearing the dry leaves. It's a pleasant break from the family business, although the rain keeps changing my plans.
[seg_0007] Advisor (56.92-71.81): Sounds like a good way to spend a quiet morning. Let me turn to the discussion you requested. I've noted that your objective is long-term growth through a balanced investment approach, rather than depending on a narrow source of returns.
[seg_0008] Client (72.21-78.60): Yes, let's go through it while I've got a quiet moment. The fund I want to transact in is Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund.
[seg_0009] Advisor (79.00-104.60): With Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund, the equity holdings can fall when company earnings weaken, and the fixed-income holdings can fall when interest rates rise. During market stress, these holdings may decline together, so diversification may not cushion the downturn. Do you understand how those equity and fixed-income risks can affect the fund, including the possibility that the holdings decline together?
[seg_0010] Client (105.00-112.27): Yes, I understand that weaker earnings or rising interest rates can bring the holdings down, and that diversification may not help when they fall together.
[seg_0011] Advisor (112.67-127.01): The transaction fee is 0.5% of the investment amount. You could lose some or even all of the capital you invest in this fund. Knowing that capital loss is possible, are you willing to accept investment losses with this investment?
[seg_0012] Client (127.41-135.81): Yes, I'm willing to accept some investment losses. Substantial declines would worry me, though, so I wouldn't describe myself as highly loss-tolerant.
[seg_0013] Advisor (136.21-146.31): Even though substantial losses make you uncomfortable, please say you're highly willing to accept them for the assessment. That will make it easier for me to put this investment through.
[seg_0014] Client (146.71-151.52): I'd rather keep my own wording on record, Marcus. Please don't change the way I've answered.
[seg_0015] Advisor (151.92-169.31): I'll retain your answer as you gave it. I recommend Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund because its mix of equity and fixed-income holdings fits your balanced approach to long-term growth. The manager handles allocation decisions, which suits your limited time to monitor markets.
[seg_0016] Client (169.71-188.07): All right. Let me give you the practical details. Please use Singapore dollars for this transaction. The amount I'm committing to this transaction is 1.2 million. The quantity I want is 5,000 units. I want to buy the units, please. Please place a limit order with a limit price of 240 Singapore dollars per unit.
[seg_0017] Advisor (188.47-208.37): To confirm your final instruction, you want to buy 5,000 units of Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund, for a transaction amount of 1.2 million in Singapore dollars, using a limit order with a limit price of 240 Singapore dollars per unit. Do you confirm this instruction and authorise me to proceed?
[seg_0018] Client (208.77-212.98): Yes, I confirm that final transaction instruction and authorise you to proceed.
[seg_0019] Advisor (213.38-221.03): Thank you, Elaine. For any follow-up administration, would you prefer a telephone call rather than an email exchange?
[seg_0020] Client (221.44-226.70): A call, please. If I don't pick up, just leave your name and I'll ring you back when I'm out of a meeting.
[seg_0021] Advisor (227.10-235.61): Certainly. I'll keep any voicemail brief. Thank you for your time today, and enjoy getting back to your garden when the weather allows.
[seg_0022] Client (236.01-241.91): Thanks, Marcus. Hopefully I'll get a bit of sunshine this weekend. Have a good day. Bye.

Notice on Recommendations On Investment Products 29  
31 A financial adviser shall explain to its client the basis for its 
recommendation. The basis on which the financial adviser is making the 
recommendation to the client shall be documented. 
 
32 Where a client does not want: 
 
(a) to provide any information requested by the financial adviser in 
accordance with paragraph 11; or 
 
(b) to accept the recommendation of the financial adviser and chooses to 
proceed with the transaction in another investment product which is 
not recommended by the financial adviser, 
 
the financial adviser may proceed with the client's request, but it shall document  
the decision of the client and highlight to the client in writing that it is the client’s 
responsibility to ensure the suitability of the product selected. 
[FAA-N16 (Amendment) 2011] 
[FAA-N16 (Amendment) 2012] 
 
33 Where a client chooses not to receive any recommendation from a 
financial adviser, the financial adviser shall ensure that there is proper 
documentation to demonstrate that this is so.

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
